In mathematics, a '''Rothberger space''' is a [[topological space]] that satisfies a certain a basic [[selection principle]]. A Rothberger space is a space in which for every sequence of open covers <math>\mathcal{U}_1, \mathcal{U}_2, \ldots</math> of the space there are sets <math> U_1 \in \mathcal{U}_1, U_2 \in \mathcal{U}_2, \ldots</math> such that the family <math>\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}</math> covers the space.

== History ==
In 1938, Fritz Rothberger introduced his property known as <math>C''</math>.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Rothberger|first=Fritz|date=1938-01-01|title=Eine Verschärfung der Eigenschaft C|url=http://pldml.icm.edu.pl/pldml/element/bwmeta1.element.bwnjournal-article-fmv30i1p8bwm?q=bwmeta1.element.bwnjournal-number-fm-1938-30-1;7&qt=CHILDREN-STATELESS|journal=Fundamenta Mathematicae|language=DE|volume=30|issue=1|pages=50–55|doi=10.4064/fm-30-1-50-55|issn=0016-2736|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Characterizations ==

=== Combinatorial characterization ===
For subsets of the real line, the Rothberger property can be characterized using continuous functions into the [[Baire space]] <math>\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}</math>. A subset <math>A</math> of <math>\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}</math> is guessable if there is a function <math>g\in A</math> such that the sets  <math> \{n:f(n)=g(n)\}</math> are infinite for all functions <math> f\in A</math>. A subset of the real line is Rothberger iff every continuous image of that space into the Baire space is guessable. In particular, every subset of the real line of cardinality less than [[Cichoń's diagram|<math> \mathrm{cov}(\mathcal{M})</math>]]<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Nkzbkj-c83YC|title=Set Theory: On the Structure of the Real Line|last1=Bartoszynski|first1=Tomek|last2=Judah|first2=Haim|date=1995-08-15|publisher=[[Taylor & Francis]]|isbn=9781568810447|language=en}}</ref> is Rothberger.

=== Topological game characterization ===
Let <math>X</math> be a topological space. The Rothberger game <math>\text{G}_1(\mathbf{O},\mathbf{O})</math> played on <math>X</math> is a [[topological game]] with two players Alice and Bob.

'''1st round''': Alice chooses an open cover <math>\mathcal{U}_1</math> of <math>X</math>. Bob chooses a set <math>U_1\in \mathcal{U}_1</math>.

'''2nd round''': Alice chooses an open cover <math>\mathcal{U}_2</math> of <math>X</math>. Bob chooses a set <math>U_2\in\mathcal{U}_2</math>.

'''etc.'''

If the family <math>\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}</math> is a cover of the space <math>X</math>, then Bob wins the game <math>\text{G}_1(\mathbf{O},\mathbf{O})</math>. Otherwise, Alice wins.

A player has a winning strategy if he knows how to play in order to win the game <math>\text{G}_1(\mathbf{O},\mathbf{O})</math> (formally, a winning strategy is a function).
* A topological space is Rothberger iff Alice has no winning strategy in the game <math>\text{G}_1(\mathbf{O},\mathbf{O})</math> played on this space.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Pawlikowski|first=Janusz|title=Undetermined sets of point-open games|url=https://eudml.org/doc/212029|journal=Fundamenta Mathematicae|date=1994 |volume=144|issue=3|pages=279–285 |doi=10.4064/fm-144-3-279-285 |issn=0016-2736}}</ref>
* Let <math>X</math> be a metric space. Bob has a winning strategy in the game <math>\text{G}_1(\mathbf{O},\mathbf{O})</math> played on the space <math>X</math> iff the space <math>X</math> is countable.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Scheepers|first=Marion|date=1995-01-01|title=A direct proof of a theorem of Telgársky|url=http://www.ams.org/proc/1995-123-11/S0002-9939-1995-1273523-1/|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|volume=123|issue=11|pages=3483–3485|doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1995-1273523-1|issn=0002-9939|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Telgársky|first=Rastislav|date=1984-06-01|title=On games of Topsoe|url=http://www.mscand.dk/article/view/12050|journal=Mathematica Scandinavica|volume=54|pages=170–176|doi=10.7146/math.scand.a-12050|issn=1903-1807|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Properties ==
* Every countable topological space is Rothberger.
* Every [[Luzin set]] is Rothberger.<ref name=":1" />
* Every Rothberger subset of the real line has [[Strong measure zero set|strong measure zero]].<ref name=":1" />
* In the [[Laver model]] for the consistency of the [[Strong measure zero set|Borel conjecture]] every Rothberger subset of the real line is countable.
